items.title: Dick Katz interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002
items.q: Danny Kaye had a terrific arrangement, I forget which tune, it might have been “Sandman” or something, and they had that [scats Basie ending] and I refused to play it.

ctx.x: Do what the producer says. Very often. They don’t want any trouble. It didn’t make that much difference for something like that. You know Tyree Glen would have said play Count Basie. The one time I rebelled at the end of a Warner — Danny Kaye had a terrific arrangement, I forget which tune, it might have been “Sandman” or something, and they had that [scats Basie ending] and I refused to play it. I played the rhythm but I changed the voicing. I just couldn’t bring myself to do it. Because even then it was like…
I guess. And it always will be.
